statement: We use the following form of Grothendieck's three axioms. A class $W$ of functors in $\Cat$ is a fundamental localizer if it satisfies LF1--LF3. LF1 means that identities belong to $W$, that $W$ has the two-out-of-three property, and that whenever $i:X\to Y$ and $r:Y\to X$ satisfy $ri=\id_X$ and $ir\in W$, then $r\in W$. LF2 says that $A\to e$ belongs to $W$ whenever $A$ has a terminal object. LF3 says that for a commutative triangle $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C$, if every functor $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ belongs to $W$, then $u\in W$. Here both slices use the indicated functors to $C$. A category is $W$-aspherical when its unique functor to $e$ belongs to $W$.
notes: Known: fundamental localizer source_label=A:localizer Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For a presheaf $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, write $U/H$ for its category of elements: its objects are $(u,h)$, and a morphism $(u,h)\to(v,k)$ is an arrow $a:u\to v$ with $H(a)k=h$. Given $p:U\to U'$, the functor $p_!:\Set^{U^{\op}}\to\Set^{U'^{\op}}$ is ordinary left Kan extension along $p^{\op}$. The presheaf $H$ is totally $W$-aspherical if $U'/p_!H$ is $W$-aspherical for every small $U'$ and every $p$. A category $A$ is totally $W$-aspherical if its terminal presheaf $1_A$ is so. We denote this property by $T_W(A)$. For $f:X\to Y$, put $H_y(x)=\Hom_Y(fx,y)$. The functor $f$ is \emph{strictly} $W$-aspherical if every presheaf $H_y$ is totally $W$-aspherical, and \emph{totally} $W$-aspherical if every category $X/y=X/H_y$ satisfies $T_W$. For a sieve $i:U\hookrightarrow X$, let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve on the objects $x$ for which some arrow $u\to x$, $u\in U$, exists. The sieve is $W$-dwy\'erienne, respectively totally $W$-dwy\'erienne, if $U\to\overline U$ is strictly, respectively totally, $W$-aspherical. A cosieve has either property when its opposite sieve has that property.
notes: Known: manuscript Definitions 1 and 2 source_label=A:definitions Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For $f:A\to B$, define the presheaf $P_f:B^{\op}\to\Set$ by \[ P_f(b)=\pi_0(b\backslash A). \] There is a canonical factorization in $\Cat$ \[ A\xrightarrow{q_f}D_f:=B/P_f\xrightarrow{\rho_f}B, \qquad q_f(a)=(fa,[a,\id_{fa}]), \] where $q_f$ is final and $\rho_f$ is a discrete fibration. It is the factorization into a final functor followed by a discrete fibration, unique up to a unique isomorphism over $B$ compatible with the map from $A$. Moreover $P_f\cong f_!1_A$ naturally in $b$.
notes: Proved: the explicit comprehensive factorization source_label=A:comprehensive Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For any fundamental localizer $W$ and any small category $A$, $T_W(A)$ is equivalent to the assertion that every target $B$ of an ordinary final functor $A\to B$ is $W$-aspherical. If $T_W(A)$ and $A\to B$ is final, then $T_W(B)$.
notes: Proved: final-image reformulation and closure source_label=A:final-images Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$ and $\pi:U/H\to U$. For every $p:U\to U'$ there is a canonical final functor \[ q_{p,H}:U/H\longrightarrow U'/p_!H \] over $p$. In particular, $T_W(U/H)$ implies total $W$-asphericity of $H$. Total presheaves are preserved by every ordinary $p_!$.
notes: Proved: categories of elements map finally under Kan extension source_label=A:elements-Kan Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: If $A$ is nonempty and filtered and $f:A\to B$ is final, then $B$ is nonempty and filtered.
notes: Proved: final images of filtered categories are filtered source_label=A:filtered-final Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Every small filtered category is totally $W$-aspherical for every fundamental localizer satisfying exactly LF1--LF3 of Definition~A.1. No additional filtered-colimit axiom is required.
notes: Known: filtered categories are total for every fundamental localizer source_label=A:filtered Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Totality is invariant under equivalence of categories and under isomorphism of presheaves, and it passes from $T_W$ to $T_{W'}$ when $W\subseteq W'$. For $W\subseteq W_0$, it implies that the category of elements in the identity test is nonempty and connected. It is not in general invariant under $\Winfty$-equivalence, as the outgoing-fork example in the audit below shows. For the universal localizer consisting of all functors, every category and every presheaf, including the empty ones, is total.
notes: Proved: invariance that is and is not automatic source_label=A:invariance Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For a fundamental localizer $W$, the axiom called W(7 bis) at XII ms.~75--76 asserts the following biconditional for every small category $X$ covered by two full sieves $U,V$ \citep{GrothendieckDerivateursXIIb}: \[ (U\cap V\longrightarrow V)\in W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (U\longrightarrow X)\in W. \] The symmetric biconditional is included. W(7), at ms.~76--77, concerns a morphism of two such cover squares. Of the three conditions that the map on the intersection belongs to $W$, that both maps on the pieces belong to $W$, and that the map on the union belongs to $W$, any two must imply the third. These are stronger assertions than forward homotopy gluing.
notes: Known: the full gluing axioms of XII source_label=A:audit-gluing Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Full biconditional differs from forward gluing

statement: Let $U$ be a small category, $H:U^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ a presheaf, and $E=U/H$ with projection $\alpha:E\to U$. Let $X$ be the category with full sieve $U$, one complementary object $t$ with only its identity endomorphism, and crossing arrows $\operatorname{Hom}_X(u,t)=H(u)$. There is a category $M$, covered by two full sieves $M_U,M_t$ with intersection $E$, and a functor $F:M\to X$, such that \[ r:M_U\longrightarrow U\ \in W_\infty, \qquad M_t=E^{\triangleright},\qquad F\in W_\infty. \] The map $Br$ is a homotopy equivalence induced by a specified adjunction. Consequently $BX$ is the homotopy pushout of $BU\leftarrow BE\to *$.
notes: Proved: a categorical model for a one-point attachment source_label=A:audit-cylinder Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes empty presheaf and empty category

statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer satisfying the full W(7 bis), and let $U\subseteq X$ be a full sieve. Write $T=X\setminus U$, and let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve generated by $U$. The following are equivalent: the inclusion $U\to\overline U$ is $W$-aspherical; for every functor $g:T_1\to T$, replacing the complement by $T_1$ and the crossing bifunctor by $(u,s)\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_X(u,g(s))$ gives an inclusion $U\to\overline U_1$ in $W$; and this last condition holds for every point $g:e\to T$ whose value belongs to $\overline U\setminus U$. For a one-point complement, the corollary at XII ms.~85 is likewise valid under full W(7 bis): $U\to X$ belongs to $W$ if and only if $U/t$ is $W$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: Proposition 7 with its stated additional axiom source_label=A:audit-prop7 Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. All small complement-change functors quantified

statement: There is a category $A$ with $35$ objects and $159$ arrows, including identities, such that $BA$ is connected and integrally acyclic but has nontrivial fundamental group. We specify its complete finite presentation through face operators. Start with the two words \[ w_0=aaaaaBBB,\qquad w_1=bbbBABA, \] where capital letters denote inverses, with lengths $n_0=8,n_1=7$. A finite semisimplicial set $K$ has vertices $v,c_0,c_1$, edges $a,b$ with both endpoints $v$, and edges $r_{k,i}:c_k\to v$ for $k\in\{0,1\}$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/n_k$. It has triangles $t_{k,i}$ with ordered vertices $(c_k,v,v)$. If the $i$th letter of $w_k$ is the positive letter $\ell$, define \[ (d_0t_{k,i},d_1t_{k,i},d_2t_{k,i}) =(\ell,r_{k,i+1},r_{k,i}); \] if that letter is $\ell^{-1}$, define this triple to be $(\ell,r_{k,i},r_{k,i+1})$. The endpoint faces of every $r_{k,i}$ are $(v,c_k)$, and those of $a,b$ are $(v,v)$. These prescriptions satisfy the semisimplicial identities. There are no simplices above dimension two. The objects of $A$ are the simplices just listed. A morphism $\sigma\to\tau$ is an increasing injection $\theta:[\dim\sigma]\hookrightarrow[\dim\tau]$ for which $\theta^*\tau=\sigma$; composition is composition of the injections. In particular, distinct occurrences of the same face give distinct arrows. These definitions specify every object, arrow and composite of $A$.
notes: Proved: an explicit finite acyclic category with nontrivial fundamental group source_label=A:audit-acyclic Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Complete face operators and arrow/composition tables

statement: The converse ``$U\to X$ is a weak equivalence, therefore $U/t$ is weakly contractible'' fails for a finite sieve inclusion with a one-object complement. In particular $W_\infty$ satisfies neither the full W(7 bis) nor the full W(7), and Proposition~7 cannot be read with the additional axiom deleted.
notes: Refuted: the unqualified one-point converse and W(7 bis) for $W_\infty$ source_label=A:audit-prop7counter Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Finite counterexample with37 objects and231 arrows

statement: For every commutative coefficient ring $R$, the class $W_R$ of nerve $R$-homology equivalences satisfies W(7), and consequently W(7 bis).
notes: Proved: the homology localizers satisfy the full gluing axioms source_label=A:audit-homologygluing Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Commutative ring including zero

statement: For every fundamental localizer $W$, if $U/H$ is totally $W$-aspherical, then $H$ is totally $W$-aspherical. Every small category with a terminal object is totally $W$-aspherical, and every representable presheaf is totally $W$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: Propositions 8 and 9(a) source_label=A:audit-prop8and9a Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Every fundamental localizer

statement: For $W=W_\infty$, and also for $W=W_R$ with any nonzero commutative ring $R$, a union of two totally $W$-aspherical full sieves with totally $W$-aspherical intersection need not be totally $W$-aspherical, even if both pieces retract onto the intersection. In the homology case this refutes the statements under their full stated W(7 bis) hypothesis.
notes: Refuted: Proposition 9(b), its retraction repair, and the fork corollary source_label=A:audit-prop9b Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Counterexample respects full gluing axioms for nonzero W_R

statement: Let $A$ be small and $K:A\to\Set$ covariant. Form the category $A_K$ by adjoining an object $x$, with $A_K(x,a)=K(a)$, $A_K(a,x)=\varnothing$, and $A_K(x,x)=\{\id_x\}$. Composition of $h:x\to a$ with $v:a\to b$ is $K(v)h$. Put $E=\El_A(K)$ and let $\pi:E\to A$ forget the element. Then $i:A\hookrightarrow A_K$ is final if and only if $E$ is nonempty and connected. Without any contractibility assumption on $BA$, there is a natural homotopy-pushout description \[ B(A_K)\simeq\operatorname{hocolim}\bigl(BA\xleftarrow{B\pi}BE\longrightarrow *\bigr). \] More precisely, the displayed realization is the mapping cone of the specified map $B\pi:BE\to BA$, not a construction determined only by the two abstract homotopy types.
notes: Proved: Lead 1, including the unrestricted homotopy type source_label=B:collage Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Suppose $BA$ is weakly contractible and $E=\El_A(K)$ is nonempty and connected. Then \[ B(A_K)\simeq\Sigma BE, \qquad \widetilde H_n(B(A_K);\mathbb Z)\cong \widetilde H_{n-1}(BE;\mathbb Z) \quad(n\geq1). \] Consequently $B(A_K)$ is weakly contractible if and only if $BE$ is integrally acyclic. In particular, if $T_{\Winfty}(A)$, every such $E$ is acyclic. The same necessary assertion with coefficients in a commutative ring $R$ holds under $T_{W_R}(A)$.
notes: Proved: the integral obstruction and its converse for one collage source_label=B:acyclic-test Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: If $T_W(A)$ and $\El_A(K)$ is nonempty and connected, then $T_W(A_K)$. This remains true after any small transfinite succession of such one-object collages, taking unions at limit ordinals. Thus every connected covariant element-category test on every category obtained in this way is a necessary test, not just those on the starting category.
notes: Proved: finite and transfinite iteration source_label=B:iteration Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $a,b:p\to q$ be a parallel pair in any small category $A$. Let $h_p=A(p,-)$ and let $H$ be the pointwise quotient of $h_p$ generated by $ca\sim cb$, for every $c:q\to r$ and every $r\in A$. Then $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ is nonempty and connected and \[ H_1(B\operatorname{El}_A(H);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/I, \] where $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is the subgroup generated by all integers $\sum_cn_c$ such that \[ \sum_cn_c(ca-cb)=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb Z[A(p,r)] \] for one object $r$ and a finitely supported family $(n_c)_{c\in A(q,r)}$. Equivalently, if $I=g\mathbb Z$ with $g\geq0$, this group is $\mathbb Z/g\mathbb Z$. This formula has no asphericity assumption on $A$.
notes: Proved: the integral formula in Lead 2 source_label=B:lead2 Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. No asphericity assumption on the base required

statement: Let $M=\{1,e,f\}$, with $1$ a unit and $uv=v$ for $u,v\in\{e,f\}$. Regard $M$ as a one-object category with multiplication $uv=u\circ v$. It is cofiltered, its classifying space is contractible, and it is not filtered. Let $K:M\to\Set$ have underlying set $\{h,i\}$, with $1$ acting identically and both $e,f$ acting constantly with value $i$. Then \[ B\El_M(K)\simeq S^1, \qquad B(M_K)\simeq S^2. \] The inclusion $M\to M_K$ is final. In particular $M$ is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical and is not totally $W_R$-aspherical for any nonzero commutative ring $R$.
notes: Proved: Lead 3 source_label=B:right-zero Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $I,J$ be nonempty small sets, let $R_{I,J}=I\times J$ with $(i,j)(k,l)=(i,l)$, and let $M_{I,J}=R_{I,J}^{1}$ have a new identity adjoined. Then $M_{I,J}$ is filtered, and totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, if and only if $|J|=1$. It is cofiltered if and only if $|I|=1$. For every nonzero $R$, total $W_R$-asphericity has the same classification. If the band is empty, adjoining an identity gives the trivial monoid and all these properties hold.
notes: Proved: the whole rectangular-band family source_label=B:bands Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Every quotient $q:A\to A/{\sim}$ by a congruence on the hom-sets, with unchanged objects, is final. Every localization $A\to A[S^{-1}]$ at a set of arrows is final. The canonical fully faithful functor $j:A\to\Kar(A)$ into its idempotent completion is final. Consequently a totally $W$-aspherical category has totally $W$-aspherical categories as all these specified images.
notes: Proved: quotient, localization, and idempotent-completion tests source_label=B:other-final Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For every fundamental localizer $W$, $T_W(A)$ holds if and only if $T_W(\Kar(A))$.
notes: Proved: totality is invariant under idempotent completion source_label=B:karoubi Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: A total category must therefore remain aspherical after every hom-set congruence and every localization, including its groupoid completion. Ordinary quotient tests do not require a faithful comparison map. Idempotent completion is stronger: it both preserves and reflects totality by the specified functors in Proposition~B.8. None of these assertions says that an arbitrary weak equivalence preserves totality. The common-successor obstruction, the affine parallel-arrow obstruction of Lead 2, and the complete element-category criterion appear in Section C.
notes: Proved: what the tests actually force source_label=B:scope-tests Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $F$ have objects $\mathbb N$ and nonidentity arrows $2r\to2r+1$ for $r\geq0$ and $2r\to2r-1$ for $r\geq1$, with no other nonidentity arrows. Then $BF$ is contractible, but $F$ is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical. Its identity endofunctor is not connected to a constant endofunctor by any finite zigzag of natural transformations.
notes: Proved: the infinite fence and the nonuniformity of contractions source_label=B:fence Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: For a small nonempty connected $A$, total $\Winfty$-asphericity is equivalent to the following condition: for every $K:A\to\mathsf{sSet}$, the canonical augmentation from its simplicial-replacement homotopy colimit to its ordinary colimit is a weak equivalence. In particular, a total category's ordinary simplicial-set colimit functor preserves all objectwise weak equivalences.
notes: Proved: homotopical ordinary colimits of simplicial sets source_label=B:homotopical-colimits Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation.

statement: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with identity. We write $\mathcal P_R(A)$ for the following property of a small category $A$: for every covariant functor $H:A\to\Set$, each connected component $E$ of the category of elements $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ is $R$-acyclic, meaning that $H_0(BE;R)=R$ and $H_j(BE;R)=0$ for $j>0$. No condition is imposed on the empty category of elements. We write $\mathcal P_\infty(A)$ when every such component is weakly contractible. These definitions use covariant, rather than presheaf, categories of elements: an arrow $(a,h)\to(a',h')$ is an arrow $v:a\to a'$ with $H(v)(h)=h'$.
notes: Proved: the action criterion source_label=C:action-definition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Exact variance and empty-element-category convention

statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a functor. If every $b\backslash A$ is nonempty and $R$-acyclic, then $Bf:BA\to BB$ induces an isomorphism on homology with coefficients in $R$. More generally, if every $b\backslash A$ is nonempty and its reduced $R$-homology vanishes in degrees $0,\ldots,d-1$, for an integer $d\geq1$, then $Bf$ induces isomorphisms in degrees less than $d$ and an epimorphism in degree $d$.
notes: Proved: homological Theorem A in the final variance source_label=C:homology-A Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Bisimplicial-chain proof

statement: If $A$ satisfies $\mathcal P_R$, then every connected component $E$ of $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$, for every $H:A\to\Set$, also satisfies $\mathcal P_R$. The corresponding assertion holds for $\mathcal P_\infty$.
notes: Proved: inheritance by categories of elements source_label=C:inherit-elements Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit coproduct-over-fibres comparison isomorphism

statement: Suppose that a connected, nonempty small category $E$ satisfies $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}$. Then $BE$ is weakly contractible. Consequently $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}(A)$ and $\mathcal P_\infty(A)$ are equivalent for every small category $A$.
notes: Proved: integral acyclicity detects every cyclic subgroup source_label=C:cyclic-covers Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Cyclic-subgroup covering test and Hurewicz

statement: For every small category $A$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical in the sense of XII, Definition~1. \item $A$ is totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical. \item $A$ is nonempty and connected, and satisfies $\mathcal P_{\mathbb Z}$. \item $A$ is nonempty and connected, and satisfies $\mathcal P_\infty$. \end{enumerate} In particular, this is a criterion in terms of all covariant set-valued diagrams on $A$, involving no quantification over target categories or final functors. Moreover every connected component of every $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ is itself totally $\Winfty$-aspherical whenever $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: characterization of total asphericity source_label=C:classification Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Complete characterization with covariant set-valued tests

statement: Let $A$ be nonempty and connected. If $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact, then $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.
notes: Proved: exact integral colimits are sufficient source_label=C:exact-sufficient Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Direct sums over element fibres preserve exactness

statement: Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ have objects $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for $n\geq0$, and all strictly increasing functions as arrows, with ordinary composition of functions. This is a countable small category. In the next construction $\mathbb Z[S]$ denotes the free abelian group on a set $S$, and the augmentation of a finite linear combination of arrows is the sum of its coefficients.
notes: Proved: the category of injective ordinals source_label=C:delta-definition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Countable small category

statement: Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be polynomials in $\mathbb Z[x_0,\ldots,x_n,u]$ such that $F_i-F_j\in(x_i,x_j)$ for every pair $i,j$. There exists $C$ in this polynomial ring with $C-F_i\in(x_i)$ for every $i$. If all $F_i$ are homogeneous of the same degree, $C$ can be chosen homogeneous of that degree.
notes: Proved: interpolation on coordinate hyperplanes source_label=C:interpolation Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit inclusion-exclusion formula

statement: For every $n\geq0$ there are an integer $M\geq n$ and \[ t\in\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}}([n],[M])] \] of augmentation $1$ such that $th=th'$ whenever $h,h':[m]\to[n]$ are parallel arrows. Here composition is extended bilinearly in the free preadditive category. For $n\geq1$ one can take $M=2^{n+1}-2$.
notes: Proved: normalized affine cones source_label=C:affine-cones Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Explicit polynomial construction; exact computational checks through dimension 3

statement: The category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical and has exact colimits of abelian-group-valued diagrams, but is not filtered. Consequently Lead~4 for $\Winfty$ and manuscript row II-C-003 have a negative answer for arbitrary small categories.
notes: Refuted: total asphericity need not imply filteredness source_label=C:counterexample Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Counterexample Delta_inj completely specified and verified

statement: A totally $\Winfty$-aspherical category $A$ is nonempty, its objects have common successors, and for every parallel pair $a,b:p\to q$ there exist an object $r$ and an integral arrow combination $t\in\mathbb Z[A(q,r)]$ of augmentation $1$ satisfying $ta=tb$.
notes: Proved: directedness and affine equalizers source_label=C:directed-affine Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Finite target consolidation proved

statement: Let $M$ be any small monoid, with multiplication $yx$ denoting composition of $x$ followed by $y$. Suppose that for every $x,a\in M$ there is $t\in\mathbb Z[M]$ with augmentation $1$ such that $tx=txa$. Then $M$, viewed as a one-object category, is filtered.
notes: Proved: a signed-measure criterion for monoids source_label=C:monoid-lemma Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Finite invariant signed measures and minimal period descent

statement: Let $A$ have a weakly terminal object $q$, meaning that $A(a,q)\ne\varnothing$ for every object $a$. Then $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical if and only if it is filtered. In particular the equivalence holds for every monoid and every category with finitely many objects, and hence for every category with finitely many arrows.
notes: Proved: monoids and categories with a weakly terminal object source_label=C:weak-terminal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes all finite-arrow categories; does not extend by an unsupported infinite-limit argument

statement: The category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is not sifted. In the category of cospans from $[0],[0]$ to a common ordinal, a cospan is an ordinal with two distinguished points. Their comparison, $<$, $=$, or $>$, is invariant under every morphism of cospans, since all transition functions are injective and increasing. Each comparison class is connected: it receives the canonical cospan on $[1]$, $[0]$, or $[1]$ respectively, by the injection selecting the distinguished points. Thus this cospan category has exactly three connected components, and the diagonal is not final. This prevents an attempted proof of the open implication in Remark~D.7 by first asserting that totality forces siftedness.
notes: Proved: the counterexample is not sifted source_label=C:not-sifted Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Its two-point cospan category has exactly three components

statement: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ with identity, let $W_R$ be the functors whose nerves induce isomorphisms on $H_j(-;R)$ for every $j\geq0$. Then $W_R$ is a fundamental localizer with the precise relative Theorem~A axiom fixed in Part~A.
notes: Proved: the homology localizer source_label=D:homology-localizer Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Relative Theorem A established by the slice Grothendieck constructions

statement: A small category $A$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if it is nonempty and connected and satisfies $\mathcal P_R(A)$ of Definition~C.1. In particular \[ \{A:A\text{ is totally }W_{\mathbb Z}\text{-aspherical}\} =\{A:A\text{ is totally }\Winfty\text{-aspherical}\}. \]
notes: Proved: total $R$-asphericity source_label=D:R-action Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Exact coefficient-ring scope

statement: For a small category $A$ and a nonzero commutative ring $R$, define $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$ to have the objects of $A$ and the morphisms \[ \operatorname{Aff}_R(A)(a,b)= \left\{\sum_{f\in A(a,b)}r_ff\in R[A(a,b)]: \text{finite support},\ \sum_fr_f=1_R\right\}. \] Composition is the bilinear extension of composition in $A$; augmentations multiply, so composition preserves augmentation $1$. Each identity is the original identity with coefficient $1_R$. This is an ordinary small category, generally not an additive category. Its connected components are those of $A$.
notes: Proved: affine linearization source_label=D:aff-definition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Ordinary category; commutative unital nonzero coefficient ring

statement: For every small category $A$, including the empty category, and every nonzero commutative ring $R$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\colim_A:(R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact. \item Every connected component of $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$ is filtered. \end{enumerate} In explicit terms, condition (2) requires common successors within each component and an augmentation-one affine equalizer for every pair of parallel \emph{affine} arrows. It is not merely the condition in Lead~2 for one pair of original arrows. For $R=\mathbb Z$ this is the Isbell--Mitchell affine criterion \citep{IsbellMitchell1973Exact,IsbellMitchell1976Fixed}; a related finite-family formulation is verified in \citet[Section~1, unnumbered theorem]{Isbell1968Exact}. We supply the proof rather than relying on an unavailable theorem number from the original AMS papers.
notes: Proved: the affine exact-colimit criterion source_label=D:affine-exactness Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Self-contained proof of the precise affine condition

statement: If $A$ is nonempty and connected and $\colim_A:(R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is exact, then $A$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical. For $R=\mathbb Z$ the conclusion strengthens to total $\Winfty$-asphericity.
notes: Proved: exact module colimits imply total homology asphericity source_label=D:exact-R-sufficient Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Integral conclusion strengthens to W_infinity

statement: Let $D$ have two objects $0,1$ and only their identity arrows. Its colimit functor on abelian groups is $(M_0,M_1)\mapsto M_0\oplus M_1$, which is exact. Nevertheless $D$ is not totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical: the identity is final and $H_0(BD;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^2\ne\mathbb Z$. The empty category provides another counterexample, with exact zero colimit. Thus the literal equivalence stated in Lead~4 is false; nonemptiness and connectedness cannot be suppressed. The finite category and its composition law are checked in \texttt{cd\_finite\_checks.py}.
notes: Refuted: the literal homology half of Lead 4 source_label=D:disconnected-counterexample Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Discrete two-object and empty categories; finite check attached

statement: The remaining implication is the precise statement \[ \left. \begin{array}{c} A\text{ small, nonempty, connected},\\ A\text{ totally }\Winfty\text{-aspherical} \end{array}\right\} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab\text{ exact}. \] Equivalently, by Theorems~C.5 and D.4, does $\mathcal P_\infty(A)$ force $\operatorname{Aff}_{\mathbb Z}(A)$ to be filtered? We have not proved this implication or produced a counterexample. This is an unresolved implication of the present work, not an assertion of a currently open problem in the literature. The attempted reduction through the acyclicity of $\mathbb Z[H]$ fails because these diagrams are not generally projective and their acyclicity does not supply acyclicity of arbitrary module diagrams. Lead~2 supplies affine equalizers of original parallel arrows, but exactness requires equalizers of all affine pairs. The proof in Lemma~C.12 bridges this gap for monoids and, by Theorem~C.13, for categories with a weakly terminal object. It also holds for $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ by its explicit affine cones. The first size not covered by the finite-object theorem is the case of countably infinitely many objects with no weakly terminal object; no particular smallest counterexample is claimed. For general nonzero $R$, the corresponding unproved necessity is $\mathcal P_R(A)$, with $A$ connected and nonempty, implying filteredness of $\operatorname{Aff}_R(A)$. Neither assertion is replaced here by its sufficient direction.

statement: Let $G$ be a small group, regarded as a one-object category. It is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if every subgroup $K\leq G$ is $R$-acyclic. If $G$ is finite, this is equivalent to $|G|\in R^\times$. In particular a nontrivial finite group is totally $W_{\mathbb Q}$-aspherical but is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical.

statement: For an integer $n\geq0$, $W_n$ denotes functors inducing bijections on connected components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups in degrees $1,\ldots,n$, at every basepoint. Thus $W_0$ tests only components. A category is $W_n$-aspherical precisely when its classifying space is nonempty and $n$-connected. These are fundamental localizers: weak saturation and the terminal-object axiom are immediate, and the relative axiom follows by applying $n$-truncation to the two bisimplicial comparisons used in Proposition~D.1. The functor to $n$-types is left adjoint to inclusion \citep[Proposition~5.5.6.18]{Lurie2009HTT} and consequently preserves homotopy colimits in the category of $n$-types, so an objectwise $W_n$-equivalence induces a $W_n$-equivalence on those comparisons.

statement: An ordinary final functor $f:A\to B$ induces a bijection on components and, on each component with a chosen object $a_0$, an epimorphism \[ \pi_1(BA,a_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(BB,f(a_0)). \]

statement: A small category is totally $W_0$-aspherical if and only if it is nonempty and connected. It is totally $W_1$-aspherical if and only if its classifying space is nonempty and simply connected.

The same equivalence holds for every category with finitely many objects, including the empty category by separate inspection. It fails for $n=1$: the contractible nonfiltered right-zero monoid of Part~B is totally $W_1$-aspherical.

statement: If $W\subseteq V$ are fundamental localizers, every totally $W$-aspherical category is totally $V$-aspherical. In particular every totally $\Winfty$-aspherical category is totally $W$-aspherical for every fundamental localizer satisfying exactly the axioms fixed in Part~A. Total $\Winfty$-asphericity is not invariant under a weak homotopy equivalence of categories.

statement: If the zero ring is allowed, every homology group with its coefficients is zero, so $W_R$ is the class of all functors and every small category, including the empty category, is totally $W_R$-aspherical. Its module category is the zero category, and every colimit functor is exact. The nonzero hypothesis in the preceding affine and connectedness criteria is therefore necessary. The ring-theoretic statements above have been stated for commutative unital rings; no unannounced extension of their affine-linearization proof to noncommutative coefficients is being used.

statement: If $A$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, then $\colim_A:\Set^A\to\Set$ preserves monomorphisms. Moreover every span $a\xrightarrow{f}b$, $a\xrightarrow{g}c$ in $A$ has a commuting completion: there are $u:b\to d$, $v:c\to d$ with $uf=vg$.
notes: Proved: preservation of monomorphisms of set diagrams source_label=D:set-monos Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Complete proof using directed element categories

statement: Let $A$ be totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, and let $H:A\to\Set$ have a nonempty connected category of elements. Every natural endomorphism $\tau:H\to H$ fixes an element: there are $a\in A$ and $h\in H(a)$ with $\tau_a(h)=h$.

statement: The fixed-point condition of Proposition~D.17, for all connected representations, is strictly weaker than exactness of abelian colimits. A small connected counterexample is constructed in \citet[Part~C, Construction~C.1 and Theorem~C.2, pp.~384--389]{AdamekKoubekReiterman1981Embeddings}. Their Section~A.4, p.~370, explicitly corrects the earlier identification of these conditions. In particular, the statement in \citet[Section~II.3, p.~100]{AdamekReiterman1976SetColim} cannot be used as an exactness criterion. The 1981 counterexample has the fixed-point property but fails simultaneous affine equalization of three specified parallel arrows. This source correction does not resolve Remark~D.7: we have not proved that the published counterexample satisfies $\mathcal P_\infty$. The distinction between pairwise and simultaneous affine equalization remains essential.

statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer with $W_1\subseteq W$. For every small category $A$, including the empty category, \[ T_W(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\to e\in W. \] Equivalently, every ordinary final functor whose source is $W$-aspherical has a $W$-aspherical target. By Proposition~F.28, the assumption on $W$ is precisely that $S^2$ be $W$-aspherical; it imposes no accessibility condition.
notes: Proved: totality above the one-type localizer source_label=D:sphere-totality Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes the empty category; no accessibility hypothesis

statement: Under the same hypothesis on $W$, for every small $U$ and every presheaf $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, the following are equivalent: \[ H\text{ is totally }W\text{-aspherical},\qquad U/H\text{ is }W\text{-aspherical},\qquad T_W(U/H). \] These equivalences include the empty presheaf. Strictly and totally $W$-aspherical functors coincide, and the $W$-dwy\'erienne and totally $W$-dwy\'erienne sieve classes coincide.

above the one-type localizer source_label=D:sphere-presheaves Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Includes empty presheaves; strict and total functor and sieve classes coincide

statement: Fix a fundamental localizer $W$ with $W_1\subseteq W$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The $W$-dwy\'erienne sieves are closed under composition. \item The totally $W$-dwy\'erienne sieves are closed under composition. \item Every nonempty small category is $W$-aspherical. \end{enumerate} When these conditions hold, every full sieve belongs to both classes. If condition~3 fails, the failure of composition can be witnessed by a classical Dwyer first factor and a second factor obtained by adjoining one terminal object, as in Theorem~F.9.

statement: Let $C$ be small, let $c\in C$, and let $d:c\to c$ satisfy $d^2=d$. Define \[ Q_d(v)=\{\alpha:v\to c\mid d\alpha=\alpha\}. \] This is a split subpresheaf of $C(-,c)$, with retraction $\alpha\mapsto d\alpha$. Its category of elements $C/Q_d$ is filtered and has contractible classifying space.

statement: Let $U$ be the one-object category with endomorphism monoid $\{1,e\}$, $e^2=e$. Let $R=U(-,*)$, let $Q=\{e\}\subset R$, and form the pushout of presheaves \[ H=R\amalg_QR. \] Explicitly $H(*)=\{i,h_1,h_2\}$, and $H(e)$ is the constant function with value $i$. Then $H$ is totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, and consequently totally $W$-aspherical for every fundamental localizer $W$. The category $E=U/H$ is not totally $\Winfty$-aspherical, is not totally $W_R$-aspherical for any nonzero commutative ring $R$, and is not filtered. Thus the converse of manuscript Proposition~8 is false, even for a finite category with two arrows and a three-element presheaf.

For every fundamental localizer in which the displayed sphere category $C$ is not aspherical, Theorem~E.3 gives a totally $W$-aspherical presheaf whose category of elements is not totally $W$-aspherical. In particular this holds for $\Winfty$, every nonzero homology localizer $W_R$, and every truncation localizer $W_n$ with $n\geq2$. For $W_0$ the two notions are equivalent to $U/H$ being nonempty and connected. For $W_1$ they are equivalent to $B(U/H)$ being nonempty, connected, and simply connected.

statement: For a small $U$ and a presheaf $H$, the category $U/H$ is filtered if and only if $H$ is a small filtered colimit of representable presheaves. Hence this condition is sufficient for total $W$-asphericity of $H$ for every fundamental localizer. It is not necessary, by Theorem~E.3.

statement: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a sieve, and let $i_0:U\to\overline U$ have the codomain of Definition~A.2. There is an ind-right adjoint precisely when every $U/x$, $x\in\overline U$, is filtered. Here an ind-right adjoint means a functor $r:\overline U\to\Ind(U)$ and bijections \[ \Hom_{\Ind(U)}(y_U(u),r(x))\cong\Hom_X(u,x) \] natural in $u\in U$ and $x\in\overline U$, where $y_U$ is Yoneda and $\Ind(U)$ is the full subcategory of presheaves given by small filtered colimits of representables. Such a sieve is totally $W$-dwy\'erienne for every fundamental localizer. The converse for $\Winfty$-dwy\'erienne sieves is false, even for a finite sieve, and the converse for totally $\Winfty$-dwy\'erienne sieves is also false in general.

statement: Let $E=U/H$ and $\pi:E\to U$. For a nonzero commutative ring $R$, $H$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical if and only if $BE$ is $R$-acyclic and every connected component of \[ \El_E(L\pi),\qquad L:U\to\Set, \] is $R$-acyclic. For $\Winfty$, the corresponding criterion is that $BE$ is weakly contractible and these same components are integrally acyclic. The restriction that the action factors through $\pi$ is essential; Theorem~E.3 disproves removing it.

statement: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a full sieve of small categories, let $T=X\setminus U$, and let $\overline U$ be the full cosieve generated by $U$. For $t\in T$ put \[ H_t:U^{\op}\longrightarrow\Set,\qquad H_t(u)=\Hom_X(u,t). \] The immersion is $W$-dwy\'erienne if every nonempty $H_t$ is a totally $W$-aspherical presheaf. It is totally $W$-dwy\'erienne if every nonempty $U/t$ is a totally $W$-aspherical category. These are precisely the conditions that $U\to\overline U$ be strictly, respectively totally, $W$-aspherical in XII ms.~109. A classical Dwyer map additionally requires that $U\to\overline U$ have a right adjoint. A $W$-cofibration is a functor $i:U\to X$ such that \[ i_!:U\backslash\Cat\longrightarrow X\backslash\Cat, \qquad (U\to C)\longmapsto(X\to X\amalg_U C), \] preserves morphisms whose underlying functors belong to $W$.

statement: Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer. Both classes of dwy\'erienne sieves in Definition~F.1 are stable under arbitrary cobase change in $\Cat$. Every $W$-dwy\'erienne sieve is a $W$-cofibration. In a pushout square \[ \begin{tikzcd} U\arrow[r,"i",hook]\arrow[d,"p"']&X\arrow[d,"q"]\\ C\arrow[r,"i'",hook]&X\amalg_U C, \end{tikzcd} \] the implications $p\in W\Rightarrow q\in W$ and $i\in W\Rightarrow i'\in W$ hold. The assertions apply to arbitrary small $C$ and arbitrary $p$, with no injectivity or fullness assumption on $p$.

Th\'eor\`eme~3 source_label=F:pushout Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. All categories are small; p is arbitrary, without fullness or object-injectivity assumptions. Uses only forward gluing, not full W(7) or W(7 bis).

setting source_label=F:couniversal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. The general-W proof uses Thomason factorization and Cisinski’s corrected retract statement. The equivalence is not asserted for an arbitrary weakly saturated class lacking the localizer axioms.

Under the full axiom W(7 bis) of XII ms.~76, the following conditions are equivalent: \[ i\in W,\qquad i'\in W,\qquad (\dot T\hookrightarrow T)\in W,\qquad i\text{ is a couniversal }W\text{-equivalence}. \] Under the full axiom W(7) of XII ms.~77 one also has $p\in W\Longleftrightarrow q\in W$. The equivalence between the first and last conditions requires neither additional axiom.

Every nonempty cosieve in such a category is totally $W$-aspherical. If $B$ and every value of a small covariant functor $D:B\to\Cat$ are totally $W$-aspherical, then $\int_BD$ is totally $W$-aspherical.

immersions for weak and homological equivalences source_label=F:total-composition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. statement: If $f:X\to Y$ is strictly $W$-aspherical, restriction $f^*:Y^{\wedge}\to X^{\wedge}$ takes totally $W$-aspherical presheaves to totally $W$-aspherical presheaves. Consequently strictly $W$-aspherical functors are closed under composition for every fundamental localizer $W$.

localizer source_label=F:strict-composition Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. The proof works with a collage of Kan-extended restricted representables. It does not identify total presheaves with total categories of elements and does not by itself prove sieve composition.

statement: For every fundamental localizer $W$, totally $W$-aspherical functors are closed under composition. For a small covariant diagram $D:B\to\Cat$, if $B$ and every $D(b)$ are totally $W$-aspherical, then $\int_BD$ is totally $W$-aspherical.

fundamental localizer source_label=F:total-functor-general Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. For total f and g, f_z:(gf)/z→Y/z has slices exactly X/y, so is total and hence strict. Pullback of the total terminal presheaf proves the composite total. For Grothendieck closure, the fibre inclusion D(b)→(∫D)/b is a right adjoint and ordinary final. This resolves total-functor composition for all fundamental localizers.

For $W_n$ with $n\geq2$, composition of totally $W_n$-dwy\'erienne sieves holds whenever both inclusions are between finite categories (finitely many arrows).

total sieve composition source_label=F:total-sieve-cosieves Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Sufficiency applies the cosieve condition to the support in X/y and uses a Grothendieck construction. The finite-category clause does not assert the same conclusion for categories with only finitely many objects but infinitely many arrows.

In each case there is a finite counterexample whose first factor is classical Dwyer, whose second factor is totally $W$-dwy\'erienne, and whose final target has six objects. Thus the assertion of total sieve composition for every fundamental localizer is false, whereas total functor composition holds by Theorem~F.8.

immersions source_label=F:strict-sieve-homology Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. statement: For a small category $A$, let $\operatorname{disc}A$ denote the simplicial category with its hom sets regarded as discrete simplicial sets. A functor $i:U\to X$ is discretely flat if \[ \operatorname{disc}X\amalg_{\operatorname{disc}U}(-) \] preserves Dwyer--Kan equivalences of simplicial categories under $\operatorname{disc}U$. It is a discretely flat cofibration when it is also injective on objects, and a discretely flat inclusion when it is also faithful. These are \citet[Definition~3.4]{F_HORR2024}. A sieve satisfies both extra injectivity conditions.

statement: Let $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$, put $E=U/H$, and let $\pi:E\to U$ be the projection. statement: Let $H:U^{\op}\to\Set$ be any presheaf on a small category, and let $X$ be obtained by adjoining one object $t$, with $X(u,t)=H(u)$, no arrows from $t$ to $U$, and only the identity endomorphism of $t$. Then $U\hookrightarrow X$ is a couniversal $W_\infty$-equivalence if and only if $H$ is totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical. For a nonzero commutative unital ring $R$, it is a couniversal $W_R$-equivalence if and only if $H$ is totally $W_R$-aspherical.

Proved: the exact one-point couniversality
criterion source_label=F:onepoint-couniversal Statement field preserves LaTeX mathematical notation. Relative homology proves necessity and the W_R equivalence, including exclusion of empty weights. statement: Let $n\geq2$, let \[ I=\Phi_n=(0\to1\leftarrow2\to\cdots\leftarrow2n), \qquad j:\{0,2n\}\hookrightarrow I, \] and let $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow[1]$ select the initial object. statement: Fix $n\geq2$ and the endpoint inclusion $j$ above. Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer for which $S^2$ is not $W$-aspherical. If a class $\mathcal K$ of full sieve inclusions consists of $W$-cofibrations and is closed under $i\mapsto i\mathbin{\square}j$, then every member of $\mathcal K$ is an isomorphism. In particular there is no nontrivial class satisfying C048 for $W_\infty$, for $W_R$ with a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, or for $W_m$ with $m\geq2$. The class of isomorphisms satisfies the conditions literally and is the maximal possible class.

statement: For $W_0$, every functor is a $W_0$-cofibration. For $W_1$, every object-injective functor is a $W_1$-cofibration. Consequently all full sieve inclusions form a class satisfying C048 for each of $W_0$ and $W_1$.

statement: The following five assertions, each quantified over all small categories and all indicated presheaves, are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item Every $W_\infty$-dwy\'erienne sieve is discretely flat. \item $W_\infty$-dwy\'erienne sieves are closed under composition. \item Every totally $W_{\mathbb Z}$-aspherical presheaf is totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. \item If $H$ is a totally $W_\infty$-aspherical presheaf on $U$ and $V\subset U$ is a full cosieve with $H|_V$ nonempty, then $H|_V$ is totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. \item Every couniversal $W_\infty$-equivalence which is a full sieve whose complementary full category is isomorphic to $e$ (one object and only its identity) is $W_\infty$-dwy\'erienne. \end{enumerate} If assertion~2 fails, a counterexample can be chosen with a classical Dwyer sieve as its first factor and a one-object extension as its second factor. The equivalence theorem does not decide whether these five assertions hold.

statement: The arguments in this part do not decide whether every $W_\infty$-dwy\'erienne sieve is discretely flat, nor whether $W_\infty$-dwy\'erienne sieves are always closed under composition. These are equivalent to the one-point couniversal-recognition question and the presheaf implication in Theorem~F.26. Strict and total functors compose for every fundamental localizer. For sieves, the universal assertion of composition is false by Theorem~F.10; total composition for a fixed localizer is characterized exactly by Theorem~F.9. For finite $n\geq2$, strict $W_n$-dwy\'erienne sieve composition, and total $W_n$-dwy\'erienne sieve composition without the finite-category hypothesis, are not settled here. The remaining $S^2$-aspherical case of C048 is settled in Corollary~F.31 below.

statement: Let $W$ be any fundamental localizer, with no accessibility assumption, and let $n\geq0$. statement: Let $Y$ be a small category and $y_0$ an object of $Y$. A type $\tau$ is a finite word in the signs $+$ and $-$. Its interval $I_\tau$ has objects $0,\ldots,n$, where $n$ is the length of $\tau$, and is the free category on the oriented line whose $i$th edge has the indicated sign. A morphism of types is an endpoint-preserving functor $\varphi:I_\tau\to I_\rho$ whose object function is nondecreasing in the numerical ordering of the vertices. This numerical ordering is distinct from the ordering defined by the arrows of the interval. An object of $P(Y,y_0)=\operatorname{Ch}(Y;y_0,-)$ is a pair $(\tau,c)$ with $c:I_\tau\to Y$ and $c(0)=y_0$. A morphism \[ (\tau,c)\longrightarrow(\rho,d) \] is a pair $(\varphi,\eta)$ consisting of such a type morphism and a natural transformation $\eta:c\Rightarrow d\varphi$ whose component at $0$ is $\mathrm{id}_{y_0}$. The composite of $(\varphi,\eta)$ and $(\psi,\theta)$ is $(\psi\varphi,(\theta\varphi)\eta)$. The endpoint functor \[ q:P(Y,y_0)\longrightarrow Y \] sends $(\tau,c)$ to $c(n)$ and $(\varphi,\eta)$ to $\eta_n$. The category $\operatorname{Ch}(Y;a,b)$ has fixed source $a$, fixed endpoint $b$, and requires the natural-transformation components at both endpoints to be identities.
